Sections.Screening_and_Comorbidities: Screening for and treatment of aetiologies and cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular comorbidities is recommended in patients with HFpEF. Diuretics are recommended in congested patients to alleviate symptoms and signs.
Sections.Prevention_of_Chronic_HF: Treatment of hypertension to prevent or delay onset of HF and reduce HF hospitalizations. Statin therapy recommended in patients at high risk of cardiovascular disease or with established CV disease to prevent or delay HF onset and hospitalizations. SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended in patients with diabetes at high risk of CV disease or with CV disease to prevent HF hospitalizations. Counselling against sedentary habit, obesity, cigarette smoking and alcohol abuse is recommended to prevent or delay HF onset.
Sections.Other_Management_Recommendations: Enroll HF patients in multidisciplinary HF management programmes to reduce hospitalization and mortality. Self-management strategies and home- or clinic-based programmes improve outcomes and are recommended to reduce HF hospitalization and mortality. Exercise is recommended for patients able to improve exercise capacity, quality of life, and reduce hospitalization.
Sections.Advanced_HF: Patients considered for long-term mechanical circulatory support (MCS) must have good compliance, appropriate capacity for device handling and psychosocial support. Heart transplantation is recommended for patients with advanced HF refractory to medical/device therapy if no absolute contraindications.
Sections.Acute_HF_Treatment: Oxygen recommended for hypoxaemia (SpO2 <90% or PaO2 <60 mmHg) to correct hypoxaemia. Intubation for progressive respiratory failure despite oxygen/non-invasive ventilation. Intravenous loop diuretics recommended for AHF with signs/symptoms of fluid overload. Thromboprophylaxis (e.g., LMWH) recommended in patients not already anticoagulated to reduce venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. Inotropic agents are not routinely recommended; used when symptomatic hypotension and evidence of hypoperfusion. Routine use of opioids is not recommended except selected patients.
Sections.Post-hospitalization_Management: Patients hospitalized for HF should be evaluated to exclude persistent congestion before discharge and optimize oral treatment. Start evidence-based oral medical treatment before discharge when feasible; early follow-up within 1–2 weeks recommended to assess congestion, drug tolerance and start/uptitrate therapy.
Sections.HF_with_Atrial_Fibrillation: Long-term oral anticoagulation recommended in all patients with AF, HF, and CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥2 in men or ≥3 in women. DOACs preferred over VKAs in HF patients except with moderate/severe mitral stenosis or mechanical prosthetic valves. Urgent electrical cardioversion recommended in acute worsening with rapid ventricular rates and haemodynamic instability. Certain antiarrhythmic agents (flecainide, encainide, disopyramide, dronedarone, and D-sotalol) not recommended due to safety concerns.

Associated Conditions: Patients with diabetes at high cardiovascular risk
genes.context: Guideline recommends SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin) in patients with diabetes at high risk of CV disease or with CV disease to prevent HF hospitalizations.
